title: "Direct Quantities and Optimization"
subtitle: "How are typed quantities evaluated without Python candidate callbacks?"

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design.

## Build one labeled Direct operator

For the declared `exp(-i omega t)` convention, the compiled operator is

$$
D(\omega)=K-\omega^2 C-i\omega G.
$$

Every entry of $D$ is serialized in coherent `siemens / second` with
dimensionality `conductance_per_time`.

The selected circuit admittance under the same convention is

$$
Y_{\mathrm{circ}}(\omega)=\frac{D(\omega)}{-i\omega}
=G-i\omega C+\frac{i}{\omega}K.
$$

For every requested ordinary frequency $f$, evaluation uses
$\omega=2\pi f$ after coherent-SI conversion.

Port loading and selected-network conversion follow the Runtime Contract.
Schur reduction, source-boundary formation, Y-to-Z conversion, and Y-to-S
conversion use factorizations and linear solves. Each solve must satisfy
$\eta(A,X,B)\le\tau(n)$ for its $AX=B$, where

$$
\eta(A,X,B)=
\frac{\lVert AX-B\rVert_\infty}
{\lVert\lvert A\rvert\lvert X\rvert+\lvert B\rvert\rVert_\infty},
\qquad
\tau(n)=256(n+1)\epsilon_{\mathrm{Float64}}.
$$

Absolute values are entrywise complex magnitudes, the matrix infinity norm is
the maximum absolute row sum, and $n$ is the square system order. Exact `0/0`
is zero; zero denominator with nonzero numerator is infinity. Operands and the
resulting residual must be finite. An empty complement that requires no solve
is a no-op. Any failed stage fails the whole grid request; no partial family,
pseudoinverse, or infinity is materialized.
These residual checks are mandatory execution-time Gates. Their raw values are
not public Result or receipt fields, and condition number is neither a Gate nor
a required computation. A verified success instead binds the exact algorithm
ID and semantic runtime source digest that performed every required check.

Each quantity Spec compiles to a typed dependency node: response element,
diagonal root, hybridized pole, transfer zero, or residue-normalized coupling.
Family-specific pole, zero, residue, response-element, and materialized-operator
mechanics belong to
[Direct Poles, Zeros, Couplings, and Operators](direct-poles-zeros-and-operators.qmd);
this page owns only the shared Direct operator/evaluation graph and CMA core.
The exact `DiagonalRootSpec` complex-Newton residual, analytic derivative,
machine-resolution certificate, and baseline-owned continuation are fixed in
[Diagonal-Root Numerical Procedure](diagonal-root-numerical-procedure.qmd).
Non-baseline ParameterSets never reselect by nearest hint or by the preceding
optimizer candidate.

## Share work inside one request

The Julia request planner deduplicates identical compile, reduction,
factorization, and root nodes. A Direct response and quantity remain distinct
public requests, but objectives within one optimization candidate share their
common dependency graph.

The `dev3` restriction to an original one-Port Direct view with no named traces
belongs only to `solve_direct`. It is neither a general View law nor an
`optimize_direct` restriction: `dev3` optimization may evaluate
`DiagonalRootSpec.frequency` and `.linewidth` on any retained View supported by
the diagonal-root procedure. A `dev3` Direct-response frequency grid is
non-empty, one-dimensional, finite, strictly increasing, duplicate-free, and
positive. A complete response Result always contains finite frequency, S, Y,
and Z arrays. Exact-open one-Port algebra is checked below this Result boundary
because its Z is not finite.

Optimization converts finite physical bounds to unit-interval coordinates,
evaluates declared normalized objectives, and keeps the CMA-ES loop entirely
inside Julia. Python's internal process layer receives completed-generation
JSONL progress; this is not a public operation keyword or callback. A candidate
whose bound values produce a singular operator, physically invalid mapped
child value, or non-continuable branch records a typed failure and `Inf` cost;
it cannot reuse a stale quantity. Invalid request schemas, mapping definitions,
or compiler invariants fail the request rather than being relabeled as bad
candidates. `Inf` is optimizer-call data only: canonical JSON records a
tagged failed-candidate penalty and never emits a non-finite JSON number.

Each active `ParameterRef` is unique. Bounds have matching dimensionality,
obey $x_{\min}<x_{\max}$, and contain the sealed baseline. The default linear
map is $z=(x-x_{\min})/(x_{\max}-x_{\min})$. Explicit `transform="log"`
additionally requires positive lower, upper, and baseline values and applies
the dimensionless coherent-SI ratio
$z=\ln(\widehat x/\widehat x_{\min})/
\ln(\widehat x_{\max}/\widehat x_{\min})$; its inverse is
$\widehat x=\widehat x_{\min}
(\widehat x_{\max}/\widehat x_{\min})^z$. Invalid bounds or baseline fail
before an attempt.

Each variable's schema keeps three distinct roles:
`model_default_bounds` is the immutable original interval,
`consumer_override_bounds` is either `null` or the consumer interval, and
resolved `lower` and `upper` are the bounds that execute. Repeated
`with_variable_overrides()` calls always retain the same original model
defaults, replace overrides for the named variables, and preserve prior
overrides for variables not named by that call. A provided
`allow_extrapolation` collection is a full replacement, never a union with
prior authorization. A freshly constructed `OptimizationSpec` serializes an
empty authorization list; every nonempty list is sorted by `ParameterRef`
identity and contains only unique active variables.

The complete optimization Spec, including those bound roles and request-local
extrapolation authorization, enters the request hash. Equivalent source-unit
spellings remain receipt-only provenance. The receipt binds the request hash
rather than duplicating a second bounds authority.

Candidate binding is ordered and fail closed: resolve the public parameter
value, check every calibration-support interval, check request-local
authorization for any out-of-support value, apply the `AffineMap`, and then
validate the mapped physical child value. Every out-of-support fan-out emits
exactly one `extrapolationEvidence` entry naming the parameter,
`consumer_target`, resolved input value, support interval, lower/upper side,
canonical distance beyond support, and authorization source. A rejected
candidate records `none`; an approved candidate records `optimization_spec`;
ordinary solve/evaluate receipt evidence records `parameter_set`. In-support
fan-out emits no entry. Distance has the input/support dimensionality and is
stored in coherent SI as `support_lower - input_value` on the lower side or
`input_value - support_upper` on the upper side; every emitted distance is
strictly positive. None claims calibration evidence outside that interval.

Failure ownership is exact. Malformed variables, bounds, objectives, selectors,
or controls raise `InvalidOptimizationSpec` before an attempt. A sealed compiler
invariant violated during execution fails the request as `CompilerInvariantError`.
After the successful baseline, an unapproved out-of-support optimizer sample is
the existing `InvalidCandidatePhysicalParameter` with
`stage="affine_support"`; it
receives the tagged positive-infinity penalty and the generation continues. A
candidate-dependent nonphysical mapped primitive value uses the same failure
type at its physical-validation stage: every bound primitive R, L, and C must
remain finite and strictly positive. Bounds may cross that physical domain,
but such a sampled candidate cannot compile. An eliminated solve, unresolved
local slope, or exhausted Newton/continuation procedure becomes
`EliminatedBlockSolveFailure`, `RootSlopeUnresolved`, or
`NumericalResolutionUnresolved`. Those candidate failures also receive the
tagged positive-infinity penalty. The same support, physical, or numerical
failure during the mandatory baseline fails the whole request. Runtime or
transport failures remain request-level `RuntimePreparationError` or
`BackendProtocolError` rather than candidate outcomes.

## Make the optimizer replayable

`CMAESSpec` defaults to `seed=0`, `max_evaluations=200`,
`population_size=None`, and `initial_sigma=0.25`. For $n$ variables the default
population is $4+\lfloor3\ln n\rfloor$. The baseline maps to the initial mean,
is evaluated once before generation 1, consumes budget, and may win.

The first slice pins
[CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl 0.2.6](https://github.com/jbrea/CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl/tree/v0.2.6),
registry tree `6bf0985be2c5ea58305d2d04e336684f64fdc12a`. Its public
`minimize()` initializes the covariance to

$$
C_0=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\exp(10^{-4}i/n)\right),
\qquad i=0,\ldots,n-1,
$$

not exact identity. That package behavior is part of the optimization
algorithm identity.

SCNSim first maps physical values to $z\in[0,1]$, calls
`minimize(objective, baseline_z, initial_sigma, ...)`, passes
`lower=zeros(n)` and `upper=ones(n)`, and lets the package apply its one
lin-quad unit-box transform in $z$ space. SCNSim does not clip, mirror, or apply
a second physical-bound transform. The exact call additionally uses
`popsize=lambda`, `maxiter=g`, `maxfevals=nothing`,
`parallel_evaluation=true`, `multi_threading=false`, `verbosity=0`, and sets
`ftol`, `xtol`, `stagnation`, `ftarget`, `maxtime`, and `noise_handling` to
`nothing`. Its internal callback captures generation evidence and emits
progress without changing sampling or stopping; ledger sealing follows the
post-update continuation boundary defined below. The signed Int64 seed
is passed as the UInt64 with the same bits; the package then constructs its
pinned `MersenneTwister`. An explicit
population is an integer of at least two, and `initial_sigma` is positive and
finite.

The request constants are
`algorithm_id="scnsim.direct_cmaes.cmaes_jl_0_2_6_state_replay.v2"` and
`box_transform_id="cmaes-jl-0.2.6-linquad-unit-box.v1"`. Reusing either string
for changed sampling, update, transform, replay, or stop semantics is invalid;
that change requires a new ID. The outer algorithm ID is a transitive binding:
it includes the exact package release and registry tree, Julia patch, call and
stop configuration, box transform, candidate compile/Direct/objective
algorithm IDs, raw/transformed hash encoding, continuation-certificate
projection and boundary timing, replay checks, and winner/tie rule. A change to
any of those dependencies requires another outer ID rather than silently
preserving `.v2`.

Only complete generations count:

$$
g=\left\lfloor\frac{B-1}{\lambda}\right\rfloor,\qquad g\ge1.
$$

Candidate failure and cache reuse still consume population ordinals. Exact
cost ties resolve by the earliest baseline/generation/population ordinal. The
`dev3` candidate supports any number of primitive R/L/C parameters and
objectives, with `DiagonalRootSpec.frequency` and `.linewidth` selectors on a
supported retained View.

`dev5` adds the schema-backed selectors
`HybridizedPoleSpec.frequency`/`.linewidth`, `TransferZeroSpec.frequency`,
`ResidueNormalizedCouplingSpec.magnitude`, and
`ResponseElementSpec.magnitude`/`.real`/`.imag`. `QuantitySum` remains legal
only as the `quantity` inside a `CostObjective`; it is not a standalone
quantity request or a new scalar selector. This selector expansion reuses the
identical CMA replay, generation-ledger, candidate-cache, winner/tie, and retry
semantics above and below; it changes no CMA numerical behavior or algorithm
identity.

The candidate cache is request-local and keyed by the exact canonical resolved
`ParameterSet` plus the selected View/objective dependency identity. It may
reuse only a typed outcome from the current verified ledger chain; it never
imports a nearby candidate or another request. The new population position is
still recorded as a cache hit with its own evaluation ordinal.

## Resume only complete generations

Every verified generation ledger contains its population, the callback-visible
raw CMA sample columns as `optimizer_latent_coordinates_f64`, the transformed
unit-box columns as `optimizer_coordinates_f64`, physical ParameterSets,
objective components, and failures in an append-only ledger. Both coordinate
arrays have length $n$ and use request-variable order within each population
column; candidate records remain in population-column order.

The canonical raw `[n, lambda]` matrix hashes to
`raw_optimizer_population_sha256`; the canonical transformed matrix hashes to
`transformed_optimizer_population_sha256`. Both hashes cover the declared
shape, population-column order, and exact Float64 bits, and must reproduce the
candidate arrays in the same ledger. The raw hash binds callback-visible $y$;
the transformed hash binds the $z$ actually consumed by physical evaluation.
Neither may be inferred from the other or from rounded physical values.

Each successful objective component records its evaluated Quantity, signed
normalized residual, and weighted cost; the request-owned target, resolved
scale/source, and weight therefore reproduce both the component and total cost.
It contains exactly $\lambda$ population outcomes in column order, with their
global evaluation ordinals; the successful baseline outcome is stored once in
the optimization Result rather than repeated in every generation.
An interrupted generation is discarded and deterministically replayed. Resume
requires exact Plan, request, algorithm, seed, controls, normalization, runtime,
and completed-ledger identity. No public resume switch changes those rules.

Before a retry starts, Python selects the verified compatible ledger with the
greatest completed generation and records its exact attempt and ledger hash in
the new attempt. Equal-generation ledgers must have identical hashes; a
disagreement is corruption, not a tie to resolve by recency. With no compatible
ledger, the request starts from its declared seed.

Julia does not serialize or restore the package's private `Optimizer` object.
It starts the exact pinned call again from the request seed. For every already
sealed generation, the batch objective verifies each transformed unit-box
Float64 bit pattern, generation, and population column before returning the
sealed costs without executing candidate physics. The package callback then
verifies every raw `y` Float64 bit pattern before the package updates its mean
or covariance. This second check is required because the lin-quad transform is
many-to-one. The first unsealed generation resumes real evaluation. Any replay
mismatch is `EvidenceIntegrityError`, not a population to accept or a reason to
fall back to physical-value round-tripping.

The callback runs before the package's `update!`, so callback evidence alone
does not make that generation resumable. Every verified generation ledger also
carries a `continuation_certificate` with projection ID
`cmaes-jl-0.2.6-julia-1.12.6-continuation-state.v1`. Its `state_sha256` hashes a
canonical JSON projection of every dynamic field that can affect a later
sample, update, or enabled stop:

- `Parameters.n`, `Parameters.λ`, `Parameters.mean`; every field of `Sigma`;
  every field of `Covariance`, including `C.mat`, eigenvalues, eigenvectors,
  and square roots; all recombination weights; box-constraint vectors; seed,
  execution flags, and the fixed `nothing` noise state;
- `Stop.it`, `Stop.maxiter`, and `Stop.reason`; wall-clock `t0` and logger state
  are excluded because `maxtime`, `ftol`, `stagnation`, `ftarget`, and `xtol`
  are all disabled and SCNSim selects the winner from its own ledger;
- every Julia 1.12.6 `MersenneTwister` field: seed, the DSFMT Int32 state
  words in `state.val`, `vals`, `ints`, `idxF`, `idxI`, `adv`, `adv_jump`,
  `adv_vals`, and `adv_ints`; and
- for a nonterminal boundary, both the next callback's raw `y` and transformed
  `z` matrices with shape `[n, lambda]`, generation, and population-column
  order.

Float64 values use the canonical 16-digit bit encoding, Int32/UInt64/UInt128
values use fixed-width two's-complement or unsigned lowercase hexadecimal, and
remaining signed integers use canonical decimal strings. Vectors use their
declared order and square matrices use row order followed by column order. The
certificate is a continuation-integrity comparison only, not an independently
reconstructable state artifact; SCNSim never restores this projection or a
private package object. Its discriminator, projection ID, field set, and array
order are versioned with the optimization algorithm ID.

A nonterminal certificate also carries
`next_raw_optimizer_population_sha256` and
`next_transformed_optimizer_population_sha256`, computed from the exact next
$y$ and $z$ matrices in that projection. A terminal certificate forbids both
fields because no next population exists. These hashes are distinct from the
generation ledger's current-population hashes; together they make the delayed
boundary check explicit without serializing a private `Optimizer`.

Because the only public hook is pre-update, generation $k<g$ becomes verified
at callback $k+1$, before `update!(k+1)`, with boundary
`post_update_post_next_sample_pre_next_update`. The projection contains
post-update-$k$ numerical state, the RNG after sampling generation $k+1$, and
the exact raw/transformed next population whose hashes the certificate names.
If an attempt ends before this boundary, generation $k$ remains unverified and
retry falls back to the preceding ledger. Generation $g$ is verified only after
`minimize()` returns with boundary `terminal_post_update`, `Stop.it=g`,
`Stop.reason=:maxiter`, its post-update state, and no next-population hash.
During retry, the batch objective verifies transformed `z` before returning
stored costs for a sealed generation. For the first unsealed generation it
caches `z` and evaluates the physics normally; its callback recomputes the
preceding ledger's certificate from package state, RNG, raw `y`, and cached
`z`, then aborts on mismatch before the package may update or publish evidence.
A final replay must match the terminal certificate. This one-generation
evidence lag is intentional and prevents an unchecked post-update divergence
from becoming resume state.

Every candidate `ParameterSet`, including the immutable winner, carries an
empty `allow_extrapolation` collection even when the optimization request was
authorized to explore outside support. Reusing those values in another solve
or evaluate call requires a new `ParameterSet` with explicit request-local
approval. The new call creates a new exact request; reduction lineage and
extrapolation approval are never inherited implicitly.
